scope_declaration.why_this_matters: GRB 130427A is the most-analysed GRB of the Fermi era. ADS full-text 'GRB 130427A' returns 738 documents, 476 of them refereed. A complete harvest is impossible and was NOT attempted. What follows is a SCOPED harvest with the rule stated below; everything outside it is a recorded omission, never an implied absence.
inclusion_rule: (a) all refereed papers whose analysis interval could overlap our stamped window [+119.107, +178.442] s - i.e. anything about the SECOND emission episode / postburst;

(b) all refereed papers that perform GBM (or GBM+LLE/LAT) prompt spectroscopy of this burst, latest-first per Phase 3b, kept even when their interval is the first pulse, because they set the model-family and pile-up frame;
(c) all refereed papers that EXCLUDED this burst and said why (the exclusions are the scientifically load-bearing statements for us);
(d) catalog rows (GBM burst/spectral catalogs, LAT catalog, LLE/BGO temporal samples);
(e) afterglow / SN / VHE / neutrino papers: CATALOGUED BY NAME ONLY with module-future tags (Phase 3c), not mined.
scope_declaration.explicitly_not_harvested: the ~440 refereed papers that mention GRB 130427A as a comparison object, a data point in a population plot, or a citation in an introduction. Also not harvested: the full afterglow/SN modelling literature (>100 papers), catalogued at family level in the dossier BEYOND-PROMPT section.

papers.title: Self-similarities and Power Laws in the Time-resolved Spectra of GRB 190114C, GRB 130427A, GRB 160509A, and GRB 160625B
papers.classification: dedicated multi-burst time-resolved analysis (BdHN framework, Bayesian + DIC)
papers.coverage_label_T9: SN-rise 0-0.65 s; 'cavity' ~15-25.5 s. The UPE phase (the bright complex) was DELIBERATELY SKIPPED for this burst.
papers.verbatim_anchor: Abstract: 'The same procedure has been repeated in the case of GRB 130427A with the exception of the UPE phase, in view of a pile-up problem.' Fig. 11 caption: 'SN-rise spectrum, well fitted by a CPL+BB model, from 0 to 0.65s (t_rf ~ 0.49s); the spectral index alpha is -0.58, cutoff energy Ec is 547.59 keV, and the BB temperature is 42.63 keV in the observer's frame'; 'Featureless spectrum of the cavity emission, from ~15 s (t_rf = 11.19 s) to ~25.5 s (t_rf = 19.03 s) fitted by a CPL, with the photon index alpha is -1.52 and the cutoff energy is at 496.13 keV'.

papers.definition_note: Ec is the e-folding cutoff energy, NOT Ep: Ep = (2+alpha)*Ec. For the SN-rise, Ep = (2-0.58)*547.59 = 777 keV. Frame-align before any diff (L21).

papers.title: The First Pulse of the Extremely Bright GRB 130427A: A Test Lab for Synchrotron Shocks
papers.classification: DEDICATED prompt analysis - of the FIRST pulse, and the source everyone cites for pile-up
papers.coverage_label_T9: 0 to 2.5 s - 'The initial pulse up to 2.5 s' - explicitly the first pulse only
papers.verbatim_anchor: Abstract: 'The initial pulse up to 2.5 s is possibly the brightest well-isolated pulse observed to date. A fine time resolution spectral analysis shows power-law decays of the peak energy from the onset of the pulse, consistent with models of internal synchrotron shock pulses. However, a strongly correlated power-law behavior is observed between the luminosity and the spectral peak energy that is inconsistent with curvature effects arising in the relativistic outflow.' Main text: 'The peak flux on the 64 ms timescale is 1300 +/- 100 photons s-1 cm-2 in the 10 - 1000 keV range and the fluence, integrated over the same energy range and a total duration of approximately 350 s, is (2.4 +/- 0.1) x 10-3 erg cm-2'; 'the energy of the spectral peak in the first time bin (T0 -0.1 to 0.0 s), 5400 +/- 1500 keV, is the second highest ever recorded'; detectors: 'the GBM bismuth germanate (BGO) detector #1 (300 keV - 45 MeV) and sodium iodide (NaI) detector #6 (8 - 300 keV)'.
papers.why_it_matters: (a) it is the citation behind every pile-up exclusion of this burst; (b) its Ep-L correlation result is explicitly INCONSISTENT with curvature/high-latitude effects - which is directly relevant to the project's HLE line (handoffs_HLE_Li2021.md), for the first pulse; (c) it used NaI 6 + BGO 1, two of our four approved detectors.
papers.pdf: Skills_training/Preece_2014_2014Sci34351P_bn130427324.pdf (NEW this session, arXiv 1311.5581 - the submitted-manuscript version, 15 pp)

papers.verbatim_anchor: Table II row: '130427A 130427324 388741629.420 47.1 138.2 +/- 3.2 1 9+10+0 472.8 23.1 40.3' with columns defined in the text as 'the GRB name (column 1), the GBM trigger number and trigger time in Mission Elapsed Time (MET, columns 2 and 3), the angle to the LAT boresight theta (column 4), the GBM duration (T90) calculated in the 50-300 keV energy band and reported by [2] (column 5), the BGO and NaI detectors used for the temporal analysis (columns 6 and 7), and the detection significances in two BGO (columns 8 and 9) and in the LLE energy range (column 10).'
papers.why_it_matters: gives sigma_LLE = 40.3 (consistent with GCN 14471's ~40 sigma, INCONSISTENT with the 15 sigma Maraventano+2025 attributes to Ajello+2019 Table 2) and sigma_BGO(0.5-1 MeV) = 472.8 - the largest in their whole sample by a factor of 4. Their BGO choice is b1, ours is b1: agreement. Their NaI set 9+10+0 (n9, na, n0) differs from ours (n6, n9, na) - n0 vs n6.
papers.prompt_sections: Sect. II + Table II. Their energy-dispersion note (BGO count-rate excess ~30-60%) is a Step-1 caveat worth reading.

GCN_14487_14579_KonusWind.t0_alias: KW T0 = 07:47:09.501 UT = GBM T0 + 3.081 s. EVERY KW interval must be shifted by +3.081 s to reach GBM time.
GCN_14487_14579_KonusWind.SECOND_EPISODE_OUR_COMPONENT: 'Modelling the 3-channel time-averaged spectrum of the second emission episode (from T0+120 s to T0+250 s) by a power law with exponential cutoff model yields the photon index alpha~-1.6 and the peak energy Ep ~ 240 keV. The 20-1200 keV energy fluence measured at this phase of the event is ~9x10^-5 erg/cm2.' -> in GBM time [+123.08, +253.08] s. NOTE: no uncertainties are quoted (3-channel fit), and the '~' is the authors'.
GCN_14487_14579_KonusWind.band_ambiguity_recorded: GCN 14579 corrects 'the total K-W energy fluence and the peak flux estimations' from 20-1200 keV to 20-10000 keV. It does NOT explicitly say whether the second-episode fluence (also printed as 20-1200 keV) is covered by the correction. Recorded as ambiguous; do not silently assume either band.
GCN_14487_14579_KonusWind.energetics: main-phase fluence (2.68+/-0.01)e-3 erg/cm2, 16-ms peak flux (6.9+/-0.1)e-4 erg/cm2/s (20-10000 keV per the correction); E_iso ~ 8.5e53 erg, L_iso,max ~ 2.7e53 erg/s at z=0.34. Errors 1 sigma.
GCN_14487_14579_KonusWind.light_curve_verbatim: 'a huge multi-peaked emission complex started at ~T0, peaked at ~T0+8 s, and having a duration of ~20 s. The emission is seen up to ~12 MeV. This extremely bright phase of the event passes into a weaker decaying tail out to ~T0+120s, when the second emission episode started. It shows a FRED-like pulse, ~100 times weaker in a peak count rate than the initial complex. The decaying emission is detectable by K-W in the 20-1200 keV band out to ~T0+250s, when the instrument switched into the data readout mode.'

phase4_consensus_DERIVED_HERE.rule: Rossi+2026 Sect. 4.1 conservative procedure - take all instruments, inflate the error to cover the spread; never pick a favourite.
phase4_consensus_DERIVED_HERE.SECOND_EPISODE_OUR_COMPONENT: ONE instrument only (Konus-Wind, 3-channel, GCN 14487): Ep ~ 240 keV, alpha ~ -1.6, over GBM [+123.08, +253.08] s. There is NOTHING to average against - no multi-instrument consensus is possible for our component, and the single available number carries no published uncertainty and comes from a 3-channel fit. Any comparison must treat it as an order-of-magnitude anchor, not a measurement.
phase4_consensus_DERIVED_HERE.FIRST_PULSE_time_integrated_Ep_for_conte: GBM catalog Band 824.99 +/- 5.45 keV over [0,255] s; GBM GCN prelim Band 830 +/- 5 keV over [0.002,18.432] s; Konus Band 1028 +/- 8 keV over [+3.08,+21.77] s (20 keV-15 MeV); Toffano+2021 Band 852 +/- 6.7 keV over [3,15] s; Aldowma+2026 Band 886 +/- 11 keV over [11.23,142.34] s; Preece+2016 Ep,fluence 784 +/- 9 keV. Spread 784-1028 keV with quoted errors of 5-11 keV -> the INTER-INSTRUMENT/INTER-INTERVAL spread (~240 keV) exceeds the statistical errors by a factor of ~25. Consensus for correlation-plane use: Ep(time-integrated, first-pulse-dominated) = 870 +/- 90 keV, error dominated entirely by the spread. THIS IS NOT OUR COMPONENT and must never be diffed against our window's Ep.
phase4_consensus_DERIVED_HERE.T90_frame_note: GBM 138.242 +/- 3.238 s (50-300 keV, n6+n9+na) vs BAT 162.83 +/- 1.36 s (15-350 keV, BAT frame, MISSING the first 52 s of emission). The BAT value is LONGER despite missing the burst onset, because BAT's softer band and its slow late peak extend T95. Qin+2013's T90 ~ E^-0.20 does NOT reconcile these - the component coverage differs, which dominates. Do not report a GBM/BAT duration tension.

coverage_label_T9.label: SECOND EMISSION EPISODE ONLY (the 'postburst' / 'FRED-like pulse at ~T0+120 s'). Our window contains NONE of the first pulse, none of the UPE/bright complex, and none of the piled-up interval.
names_this_component_carries_in_the_lite: 'the second emission episode' from T0+120 to T0+250 s (GCN 14487, Konus, in KW time = GBM +123.08 to +253.08 s)
'the slower, fainter peak of the GRB, about two minutes after the primary outburst' (GCN 14590, RHESSI)

coverage_label_T9.comparators: GBM T90 [4.096, 142.338] s (50-300 keV); GBM catalog flnc interval [0, 254.976] s; Konus second episode [+123.08, +253.08] s; Aldowma+2026 [11.23, 142.34] s; AGILE-GRID [+188.6, +708.6] s (after us); LAT continuous through our window, 95 GeV photon at +244 s (after us).
coverage_label_T9.consequence: our 59.3 s window straddles T95 (142.34 s): 23.2 s inside T90, 36.1 s outside it. The Konus second-episode integration is 130 s long and starts 4 s after our window opens and ends 75 s after it closes - so even the ONE published number for our component integrates 2.2x more time than we do, including a decaying tail we do not see. If the pulse is hard-to-soft, our Ep should sit ABOVE the Konus ~240 keV.

zero_paper_finding: NOT APPLICABLE in the usual sense (476 refereed hits) - but the FINDING for our component is nearly the mirror image: despite being the most-studied GRB of the Fermi era, the second emission episode [119, 178] s has exactly ONE dedicated refereed analysis (Du+2022, whose PDF we cannot obtain) and ONE published spectral measurement (Konus 3-channel, no errors, GCN 14487). Three separate refereed papers EXCLUDED the burst entirely (Ravasio+2019 pile-up; Duan+2020 brightness; Maraventano+2025 saturation) and two more analysed only the first pulse (Preece+2014; Toffano+2021). The brightest GRB in the GBM catalogue has an essentially unstudied second pulse.

issues: Du+2022 (2022ApJ...940...48D) - the ONLY dedicated analysis of our exact component - is UNREADABLE: IOP Radware captcha on both https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.3847/1538-4357/ac94d2/pdf and the ADS link_gateway PUB_PDF, and ADS lists no arXiv eprint. All statements about it here come from the ADS abstract. This is the single biggest gap in this burst's literature frame.
Liao+2025 (2025ApJ...983..130L) contains our trigger digits and was NOT fetched (PUB-only, IOP, same captcha risk; judged low-value - a null spectral-line search). Recorded as a deliberate omission.
476 refereed papers mention this burst; 15 were mined. The scoping rule is stated in scope_declaration. Anyone treating this harvest as exhaustive will be wrong.

The LLE detection significance is quoted as ~40 sigma (GCN 14471), 40.3 (Bissaldi+2015 Table II) and 15 sigma (Maraventano+2025, attributing it to Ajello+2019 Table 2). Recorded as an unresolved inconsistency (T5); not adjudicated here.
Konus's second-episode fluence band (20-1200 vs 20-10000 keV) is genuinely ambiguous after the GCN 14579 correction. Recorded, not guessed.
The GBM spectral catalog's best model has REDCHSQ = 7.25/481. AIC was deliberately NOT recomputed from the catalog for this burst (T8 judgement call, documented) - unlike the sibling-burst procedure.
Phase 1b (Scholar) was not used; the trigger conditions did not apply. Recorded rather than silently skipped.
No refereed analysis of the RHESSI data on our pulse was found, although GCN 14590 shows RHESSI resolved it in three bands and states the data are public. A genuine, checkable gap.
